reuse.why: Extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend and adds shared predicates (isDailyWeekendSkip, isWeekendOrHoliday, getWeekendAdjustedDate), but schedule-template and getNextDate do not use the new getWeekendAdjustedDate and write their own versions.

duplication.why: The skip-or-adjust pipeline exists both in getNextDate and in the server-side applyWeekendHandling, and schedule-template's getAdjustedDate is a local copy of getWeekendAdjustedDate.

placement.why: Predicates and the shift live in shared/schedules.ts, but the combined skip-then-adjust step (applyWeekendHandling) sits in server/schedules/app.ts while getNextDate re-does it in shared.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps: weekend/holiday rules, the new handler, the config type, tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: Reasonable named helpers, but the rule is assembled in three places, the template inverts isDailyWeekendSkip into getNextDate's noSkipWeekend flag, and fixed lookahead/padding constants are loosely tied to the holiday count.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts getAdjustedDate re-implements getWeekendAdjustedDate; shared/schedules.ts getNextDate applies its own skip filter and skipWeekend guard instead of the shared adjust helper.

disguised_duplication.where: getAdjustedDate in schedule-template.ts is getWeekendAdjustedDate under another name; the skip filter + adjust in getNextDate is a reshaped applyWeekendHandling.

abstraction_drift.where: holidays parameter added to getDateWithSkippedWeekend; daily-skip branches (take size, find filter, adjust guard) and the MM-DD case inside isWeekendOrHoliday; schedule-template and getNextDate bypass getWeekendAdjustedDate/applyWeekendHandling.
